guardrails: none: no citation gate, no critic, fix not forced to need approval
rationale: checkoutservice has the largest anomalies in the digest: memory up 1876% (z=+375) and CPU up 4411% (z=+220), with latency-90 up 764%, while its callees (payment, email, currency) show negligible change, so the fault originates in checkoutservice itself. Memory and CPU rose together, so mem versus cpu is ambiguous. I chose mem because it has the highest z-score, but the CPU rise could be a consequence such as GC pressure, or the primary fault, and no logs are available to separate them.

proposed_fix.description: Restart or roll the checkoutservice pods to reclaim memory, and set a memory limit. Then inspect the heap or profile for a leak or runaway allocation. The restart is non-destructive because the service is stateless and the pods are rescheduled.
